findings.summary: Subagent/runtime reaper goroutines leak on two NewContainer constructor error paths.
evidence: go vet flags both cancel funcs directly: stopReaper (line 1162) and stopRuntimeReaper (line 1182) not used on all paths.
Two confirmed early-return paths (container.go:1242, 1246) return (nil, err) after the reapers are already started but before the cancel funcs are captured into the struct at lines 1398/1400.
Caller never receives a *Container on these paths, so it has no way to stop the leaked reaper goroutines.
findings.recommendation: Ensure every error return between reaper start and struct assembly also calls stopReaper()/stopRuntimeReaper(), matching the existing stopCatalog() cleanup pattern already present at both flagged sites.
findings.false_positive_considerations: If NewContainer failures are effectively fatal (process exits immediately), the leak is real but inconsequential in practice.

findings.summary: Reachable third-party vulnerability: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp v1.41.0 has an oversized-response memory-exhaustion bug (GO-2026-4985), fixed in v1.43.0.
evidence: govulncheck ./... reports GO-2026-4985 reachable via otel.Init -> otlptracehttp.New / client.UploadTraces.
findings.recommendation: Bump go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlptrace/otlptracehttp (and sibling otel modules for consistency) to >= v1.43.0. Standard dependency bump.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Reachability requires OTel export enabled at runtime and a malicious/misbehaving collector endpoint.

findings.summary: Go toolchain pinned at go 1.26.2; govulncheck reports 13 distinct reachable stdlib vulnerabilities fixed in go1.26.3-go1.26.6 (TLS, HTTP/2, html/template, textproto, x509, asn1).
findings.recommendation: Bump the toolchain/go.mod go directive to 1.26.6 (or latest patch at remediation time) as a standard patch upgrade.

findings.summary: Full-repo uncapped golangci-lint (make lint) exists and is correctly configured, but no hook or CI ever runs it — pre-commit only lints changed lines (--new), pre-push only runs tests, and there is no .github/workflows directory at all.
evidence: lefthook.yml pre-commit go-lint runs `golangci-lint run --new --timeout 30s` (changed lines only); pre-push runs only `go test ./...`.
Running `make lint` directly surfaces 2,338 issues under the project's own already-approved linter set with no enforcement point ever re-measuring it.
findings.recommendation: Architect decision: wire make lint (or a scoped subset) into a nightly/scheduled job or merge-to-main gate per the guide's Tier B suggestion, not into pre-commit/pre-push.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Possible the project plans a separate CI system outside GitHub Actions that already runs make lint; no evidence of one found in-repo.

findings.summary: gosec G304 (path traversal via variable) found at 68 production call sites outside the pathsafe.ResolveUnder forbidigo-tracked adoption scope; the tracker's forbidigo rules only enforce ResolveUnder inside internal/sandbox/, internal/mcp/, internal/service/install/.
evidence: Sampled 10/68: os.ReadFile/os.Open/os.OpenFile calls on a local path variable with no visible sanitization at the call site.
findings.recommendation: Have the architect (or the Phase-1-Wave-1 migration owner) walk the 68-site list and classify each by trust boundary (CLI-flag-driven vs. externally reachable); internal/agent/managed_* sites are the highest-priority subset (see GO-AGENT-001 for a fully-traced example).
findings.false_positive_considerations: gosec's G304 rule fires on any variable-driven file open regardless of whether the variable is already constrained; a meaningful fraction of the 68 are plausibly already safe by construction.

findings.summary: internal/api's (and internal/service's own) test suites construct many service.Container instances via NewContainer and never call Shutdown() on any of them, leaking 2 reaper goroutines per test that accumulate across the run and, under go test -race, prevent internal/api and internal/service from completing even at 2.5x the default timeout.
evidence: 288 goroutines traced to NewContainer reaper-start calls counted in the 25-minute timeout dump, up from 56 at 10 minutes.
Grepped all 6 internal/api test files calling NewContainer: every t.Cleanup closes the store, none call Shutdown() on the Container.
Confirmed NOT a production defect: cmd/nanite/main.go:747 does call container.Shutdown() on the real exit path.
findings.recommendation: Add t.Cleanup(func() { container.Shutdown() }) alongside the existing store cleanup in each of the 6 call sites; check internal/service's own test suite for a related but distinct cause (see GO-SVCCORE-006).

findings.summary: internal/service / Container struct: 60-field composition root, 31.6K prod LOC across 83 files, fan-out 64. Directly confirmed by §8.3's read: Container itself is genuinely wiring-only (2 methods), but the package's mass (real behavior) actually lives in chatServiceImpl (see GO-SVCEXEC-002), not Container.
evidence: Container has 60 fields but only 2 methods (RefreshUtilitySettings, Shutdown); NewContainer is ~1065 lines of overwhelmingly constructor calls and error propagation.
findings.recommendation: No decomposition of Container itself is warranted (it is a legitimate composition root). Focus any god-object remediation on chatServiceImpl (GO-SVCEXEC-002) and SelfToolsTransport (GO-MCPTOOL-006) instead.

findings.summary: internal/store: fan-in 30, the single most gravitational package in the codebase. §8.1 confirmed the dominant caller pattern is injecting the whole concrete *store.Store (76 direct references in internal/service alone) rather than a narrower domain interface, though two healthy consumer-defined-interface counter-examples already exist in the codebase (TrustResolver, ConsultationLogger).
evidence: 76 direct *store.Store field/parameter references counted in internal/service/*.go alone.
349 methods on *Store across 63 files backing ~25+ distinct domain areas.
findings.recommendation: Architect to identify 2-3 highest-fan-out consumer domains and evaluate a narrow consumer-defined interface only where real pain (test friction, unwanted recompilation) is identified.

findings.summary: Nearly all callers depend on the concrete *store.Store handle rather than narrower domain interfaces; 76 direct *store.Store references counted in internal/service alone (fan-in 30 overall).
evidence: Contrast: dispatch.TrustResolver and grounding.ConsultationLogger are consumer-defined narrow interfaces store satisfies structurally without importing them -- proves the pattern is known, just not the default.
findings.recommendation: Identify 2-3 highest-fan-out consumer domains and evaluate a narrow consumer-defined interface only where real pain is identified, not repo-wide.
findings.false_positive_considerations: A single shared persistence facade is a defensible, normal choice at this scale.

findings.summary: *Store's 349-method surface spans ~25+ unrelated domain concepts (sessions, agents, teams, plugins, schedules, reflexes, etc).
evidence: 349 methods / 84 exported struct types counted directly across 63 files.
findings.recommendation: Do not split merely for size; a natural side effect if GO-STORE-001 is pursued, otherwise an observation only.
findings.false_positive_considerations: File-per-domain-concept within one package is the guide's own example of a healthy large package.

findings.summary: DeleteAgentByID silently converts every GetAgent error (not just not-found) into a successful no-op, so a transient DB failure during plugin-uninstall cascade cleanup silently looks like 'already gone' with nothing logged.
evidence: agents.go:1211-1221: `a, err := s.GetAgent(id); if err != nil { return nil }` swallows any error, not just sql.ErrNoRows.
Confirmed by golangci's nilerr linter.
Real caller: Host.SweepPluginAgentProfiles (plugin-unload cascade cleanup) relies on this to know whether cleanup succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish sql.ErrNoRows (legitimate no-op) from any other error (should propagate) in DeleteAgentByID.

findings.summary: ListPluginSettings has two unchecked json.Unmarshal calls; GetPluginSettings checks the identical unmarshal on the same columns, producing inconsistent behavior for the same malformed data.
evidence: plugin_settings.go:134-135 unchecked vs :46-51 checked, same operation.
findings.recommendation: Align ListPluginSettings's error handling with GetPluginSettings's.

findings.summary: Inconsistent context.Context propagation across the package: only 22/63 files reference context.Context at all; sessions.go and agents.go (the two hottest tables) have no context-taking methods at all, while teams.go's methods all take ctx.
evidence: 231 plain DB calls vs 116 context-aware equivalents counted package-wide.
findings.recommendation: Architect decision on whether to backfill ctx through sessions.go/agents.go and the rest of the plain-DB.Query files.
findings.false_positive_considerations: May be an intentional, not-yet-reached migration backlog rather than an oversight.

findings.summary: SyncDurableAgentInstanceConfig reads-then-branches-then-writes without a transaction, unlike sibling methods that push the check into a single atomic UPDATE with a RowsAffected check.
evidence: durable_agents.go:301-367 has no Begin()/transaction wrapping the read-decide-write sequence.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate whether concurrent same-slug calls are a live risk; if so, wrap in a transaction or adopt the self-checking WHERE-clause idiom siblings already use.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Caller concurrency was not traced within budget; confidence is medium specifically for this reason.

findings.summary: Mechanical 'query -> scan-loop -> append' duplication across ~20+ list methods; 41 dupl hits confirmed inside internal/store, no shared generic scanRows helper exists.
evidence: Manually sampled 2 pairs, confirmed genuine structural duplication of the scan-N-rows-into-a-slice concept.
findings.recommendation: Optional: a generic scanRows[T any](...) helper could collapse this; every site is already individually correct.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Repeated boilerplate that is individually correct and readable is a legitimate design choice; no bug found riding on this duplication.

findings.summary: 4 exported functions confirmed dead code; one's doc comment falsely claims a live caller (internal/service/ingest.go) that does not exist.
evidence: deadcode.log confirms all 4 unreachable; whole-module grep confirms zero real call sites for any.
findings.recommendation: Owner to confirm whether skill_mode_filter.go's trio is still needed and whether ClassifySkillSource's described FE gating was ever implemented; retire or wire up.

findings.summary: Pervasive task-ID/date references (~40 CW-YYYYMMDD-NNNN, ~23 TASKS/*.md paths) embedded in permanent production comments across 25+ files.
findings.recommendation: Not a blanket removal; architect could scope a trim pass for pure task-ID citations without added rationale, keeping load-bearing invariant comments.

findings.summary: internal/config bundles three distinct concerns under one generic name: Config (reads project-root nanite.yaml), AppConfig (reads config/nanite.yaml, a different file with the same base name), and pure XDG path resolution.
evidence: config.go:122 reads './nanite.yaml'; AppConfig loads 'config/' + brand.ConfigFileName + '.yaml' = 'config/nanite.yaml' -- two different files, two unrelated structs, same base filename.
findings.recommendation: Rename one file/struct to disambiguate, or split the package along the Config/AppConfig boundary.

findings.summary: inspector.trafficLight is unreachable in production (only its own test calls it); internal/service/inspector_producers.go's trafficLightFor is a byte-for-byte reimplementation, created because trafficLight is unexported.
findings.recommendation: Export inspector.TrafficLight and have internal/service call it, removing the duplicate.

findings.summary: scanTask silently discards json.Unmarshal/time.Parse errors on metadata/created_at/updated_at during durable-recovery Restore -- a malformed row silently produces empty Metadata/zero-value timestamps with zero observability.
evidence: snapshot.go:94-121: `_ = json.Unmarshal(...)`, `t.CreatedAt, _ = time.Parse(...)`.
findings.recommendation: At minimum log a warning with the task ID on parse failure.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Sibling LocalBackend.List/Snapshot already treat similar failures as skip-and-continue without logging, so this may be a deliberate 'best-effort restore' convention.

findings.summary: OpenAI streaming aborts the entire turn on the first malformed tool-call-argument JSON (EventError then return, dropping other queued tool calls, usage, and EventDone); Anthropic's equivalent path degrades gracefully with a fallback instead.
evidence: stream.go:96-123 (OpenAI) vs stream.go:232-253 (Anthropic), confirmed control-flow divergence for the same failure class.
findings.recommendation: Architect decision on whether OpenAI's path should adopt the same graceful fallback Anthropic uses.
findings.false_positive_considerations: A comment at stream.go:104-105 suggests the early return may be a deliberate 'fail loud' choice, not an oversight.

findings.summary: DelegateAndAggregate's concurrent-worker collector can hang forever if a spawned goroutine panics before writing its result, because the collector uses an unconditional blocking receive with no select/timeout/ctx.Done, unlike its sibling DelegateTask.
evidence: delegation.go:349-386; safego.Go recovers the panic but nothing writes a fallback result to the channel.
findings.recommendation: Give the collector the same timeout/cancel select DelegateTask already uses, or have each closure's deferred recover write a synthetic error result.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Only reachable if worker.Manager.SpawnFull (or the closure) can actually panic in practice -- not independently verified.

findings.summary: Inconsistent goroutine-lifecycle tracking: ~18 safego.Go call sites are bare fire-and-forget spawns with no owner Container.Shutdown() can drain, unlike one specific wake-reactor spawn already migrated to lifecycle.Manager after a PR review flagged exactly this risk.
evidence: container.go:1133-1143's own comment documents the one fix that WAS applied; the same fix was not applied to events_composite.go/delegation.go/agent_deps.go sites.
findings.recommendation: Decide package-wide which safego.Go sites are genuinely fire-and-forget-safe vs. need lifecycle.Manager tracking like the wake-reactor got.

findings.summary: snapshotAdapterTargets is dead code, but cleanupRemovedAdapters's doc comment falsely claims a rollback snapshot pass runs before it -- the destructive cleanup (stripping content from CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) has no actual rollback safety net despite the comment's claim.
evidence: Traced the only production call path (freshScaffold): no call to snapshotAdapterTargets exists before cleanupRemovedAdapters; no Rollback function exists anywhere in the repo.
findings.recommendation: Either wire snapshotAdapterTargets back in and build the promised Rollback, or correct the comment to state no rollback exists today.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Blast radius is bounded -- only strips Nanite's own previously-written managed markers, not arbitrary user content.

findings.summary: A2A push-notification webhook URL (caller-supplied at task-submit time) has no validation -- no scheme allowlist, no private-IP/localhost block -- before an outbound HTTP request is made. Classic webhook-callback SSRF pattern.
evidence: a2a_push_notifier.go:152-166; gosec's G107 rule doesn't catch this idiom (targets http.Get/Post directly, not NewRequestWithContext+client.Do).
findings.recommendation: Validate the URL at submission or delivery time against a scheme allowlist and reject loopback/link-local/private-range hosts unless explicitly trusted.
findings.false_positive_considerations: A2A endpoint's auth boundary (whether only trusted peer agents can submit tasks) was not independently verified.

findings.summary: //nolint:gosec correctly suppresses under golangci-lint but a bare gosec binary run doesn't understand that syntax, producing one avoidable false HIGH (G404) in any raw gosec ./... run the guide itself recommends.
findings.recommendation: Note in the audit runbook that //nolint:gosec won't suppress bare gosec runs; consider adding a matching #nosec comment for consistency.

findings.summary: internal/service's own go test -race timeout is NOT the Container-reaper-leak mechanism GO-TEST-001 describes -- zero of the package's 126 test files ever call NewContainer. GO-TEST-001's recommended fix will do nothing for this package's timeout; the real cause needs separate investigation.
evidence: Exhaustive grep across all 126 internal/service test files: zero calls to NewContainer.
findings.recommendation: Investigate internal/service's -race timeout as a distinct question from internal/api's -- candidates are sheer suite size (776 test functions) x -race overhead, and/or the GO-SVCCORE-002 untracked-goroutine accumulation.

findings.summary: WithAgentCycleKindForAPI's context value is written by 2 real internal/api call sites but has zero readers anywhere -- live-but-inert plumbing, self-documented as intentional forward-looking scaffolding.
findings.recommendation: Leave as documented scaffolding, or note it explicitly in a tracking doc so it isn't mistaken for wired behavior.

findings.summary: A local `var any bool` shadows the Go builtin any type for the rest of that function's scope.
evidence: adapters.go:159,169
findings.recommendation: Trivial rename (e.g. hasManaged).

findings.summary: Several files carry 15-50 line task-ID/PR-review-history comments approaching implementation-diary territory, though each explains a real invariant rather than being pure filler.
findings.recommendation: No immediate action; candidate for a future documentation-consolidation pass.

findings.summary: generateResponse is a ~1,900-line, cognitive-complexity-458, cyclomatic-225-228, maintainability-index-0 function -- the single highest-complexity function found anywhere in this audit (~5x the next-sharpest outlier), missed entirely by the mechanical triage pass. Coverage is 36.5%.
evidence: raw/golangci-audit-complexity.log confirms cognitive 458, cyclomatic 225-228, funlen 1188, maintidx 0.

Structurally one unbroken ~970-line tool-use loop with budget enforcement, plugin hooks, telemetry, provider streaming, error/compaction recovery, and tool dispatch all inlined, despite the file having an established pattern of extracting helpers elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Architect review of whether the loop's phases can be extracted into named methods without changing the mutate-in-place state-machine shape; prioritize closing the coverage gap on error/recovery branches independent of any refactor.

findings.summary: chatServiceImpl has 52 fields and 84 methods -- more than double the guide's own god-object thresholds on both axes -- and fails the wiring-only test decisively via generateResponse and dozens of other multi-hundred-line methods implementing real behavior directly.
evidence: Field count/method count counted directly across the package's production files.
findings.recommendation: The PTY/agent-runtime session-lifecycle field cluster (7 fields, already cohesive) is the most promising extraction candidate; StreamManager is direct in-repo precedent for exactly this kind of split.

findings.summary: Team semantic routing (TeamRoutingService's entire production surface) has zero production callers -- the intended wiring point (handleLaunchTeam) shipped later but calls only LaunchTeamRun, never InstallTeamRunRouting. TASKS/teams/HANDOFF.md already names this exact risk.
evidence: Confirmed by deadcode + direct grep; ResolveLazySlot is transitively unreachable too though deadcode's heuristic doesn't catch it since its enclosing type is live.
findings.recommendation: Wire TeamRoutingService into handleLaunchTeam per the original design intent, or explicitly mark the feature as deferred/shelved in the Teams architecture doc.

findings.summary: Two near-identical 'resolve policy -> busy-check -> trigger' reactors have diverged on mechanism: resolveMessageWakePolicy uses the shared override.Resolve cascade primitive; resolveSubagentCompletionPolicy hand-rolls the identical walk independently. Self-acknowledged as siblings in the package comment.
findings.recommendation: Migrate resolveSubagentCompletionPolicy onto override.Resolve the same way its sibling was, since the two documented reasons they're separate resolvers don't require different merge mechanisms.

findings.summary: buildRepairConfig (C2 auto-repair pipeline's 4-level provider/model/timeout fallback chain) and discoverManagedDurableAgentConfigs (boot-time config loader) are both 0.0% test-covered, standing out against a package where coverage is otherwise unevenly-but-not-uniformly thin.
evidence: coverage-func.log confirms both at 0.0% against sibling functions in the same files at 77-95%.
findings.recommendation: Add targeted unit tests for both; neither requires heavy fixtures.

findings.summary: durable_wake.go:232-233's best-effort store write marks a one-shot schedule 'expired' -- the file's own doc comment says this is the mechanism preventing a documented double-fire race, but its failure is silently swallowed with no log line.
findings.recommendation: Log (not necessarily propagate) the error at this specific call site, consistent with sibling failure paths in the same file.

findings.summary: chat_reflex_dispatch.go's 99-line package header and team_routing.go's 43-line priority-clamp justification both duplicate content that also lives in the referenced task file's Work Log -- a consistent house style across this half of the package.
findings.recommendation: No specific edit proposed; worth an architect pass on whether this house style should tighten toward invariant-only comments with a pointer to the task file.

findings.summary: Autocomplete file listing walks project.RepoPath with no validation anywhere in the chain; any authenticated caller can point a project at / or $HOME and enumerate filenames/sizes/mtimes (metadata only) up to depth 8.
evidence: resolveRoot (autocomplete.go:135-164) has no validation; handleCreateProject/handleUpdateProject store RepoPath verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether repo_path should be constrained to an operator-configured allowlist of directories.
findings.false_positive_considerations: In a single-operator local deployment, 'authenticated caller' and 'the person who set repo_path' are the same person.

findings.summary: handlePlaceArtifact accepts an unrestricted StoragePath at write time with zero sanitization, unlike sibling handleUploadArtifact which correctly uses pathsafe.ResolveUnder. Not currently exploitable (download path independently confines) but has zero test coverage.
evidence: Download path confirmed hardened by existing regression test TestDownloadDoesNotLeakAbsoluteEscapingPath.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same pathsafe.ResolveUnder-based confinement at write time and add a regression test mirroring the download-side tests.

findings.summary: Catalog plugin install fetches entry.ArchiveURL via http.DefaultClient with no explicit timeout and no host/scheme restriction beyond http/https -- standard package-manager-registry SSRF shape.
findings.recommendation: Give the download http.Client an explicit timeout; consider whether catalog sources should be treated as fully trusted or need an outbound-URL allowlist.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Adding a catalog source is itself an explicit, privileged, operator-initiated action.

findings.summary: Schedule and settings field validation live in the transport layer; the schedules case is self-documented in-repo as a known, real duplication across 3 independent producers (HTTP handler, reflex hook, self-tool handler).
evidence: schedules.go:117-137's own comment already names this as a real follow-up candidate, not new discovery.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate once all three producers exist, per the in-repo comment's own proposed fix path.

findings.summary: handleListMemories caps its underlying fetch to limit+offset BEFORE applying status/q filters, then reports total as the post-filter page length rather than a real match count -- silently under-returns below the requested limit when more matches exist beyond the capped window.
evidence: memories.go:93-98 sets opts.Limit=limit+offset before filtering at :116-137; :149-151 reports total: len(out).
findings.recommendation: Push status/q filtering (and a true total count) into memory.RecallOpts/Recall itself, before the limit/offset window is applied.

findings.summary: Response/decode boilerplate duplicated across 3 parallel handler-state types; 2 are architecturally justified (different receiver types) but 3 *API-receiver call sites bypass the existing shared a.decode helper for no apparent reason.
findings.recommendation: Mechanical cleanup, low priority; fold into any future pass touching these files.

findings.summary: Harness v1 durable-agent start/resume/wake handlers are confirmed byte-for-byte duplicates (via dupl) of the native /api/durable-agents/* handlers, hand-copied rather than delegating.
evidence: dupl-flagged pairs: durable_agents.go:226 <-> harness_v1.go:411 (25 lines); durable_agent_wake.go:54 <-> harness_v1.go:437 (16 lines).
findings.recommendation: Have the Harness v1 handlers call the native handler functions (or a shared private helper) directly.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Possibly deliberate protocol-stability choice insulating an external control-plane contract from internal refactors -- no comment states this rationale though.

findings.summary: The plugin-UI static-file route hand-rolls its own Clean+HasPrefix path-confinement check instead of pathsafe.ResolveUnder -- sound against traversal but doesn't call EvalSymlinks, so a symlink inside an installed plugin's ui/ dir pointing outside its root would not be caught.
evidence: plugins.go:107-120.
findings.recommendation: Route through pathsafe.ResolveUnder(baseDir, file) for consistency and to close the symlink gap.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Requires an already-installed plugin (privileged action, subject to signature verification elsewhere).

findings.summary: 7 dupl-flagged pairs within agent_capabilities.go's 4 parallel CRUD families (known-tools/known-skills/procedures/knowledge-seeds) -- mechanical, low-risk.
findings.recommendation: Judgment call on whether a generic helper is worth the abstraction cost; not required.

findings.summary: bookmarks.go:90 uses err != sql.ErrNoRows instead of errors.Is -- would silently misclassify a legitimate not-found as an internal error if the underlying call is ever wrapped with %w.
findings.recommendation: Use errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows).

findings.summary: GUI/API plugin-catalog-install path (POST /api/plugins/catalog/install, the actual Plugin Manager UI) bypasses signature/checksum verification by default -- VerifyChecksum returns nil if no checksum specified, and the signature branch only runs if the source has a configured public key, which the default seeded 'official' catalog source does not have. Not devmode-gated -- identical in production and dev builds.
evidence: handleCatalogInstall (catalog.go:248-452): signature branch only fires if sourcePublicKey != '' && entry.Signature != ''.
Default seeded catalog source's INSERT never sets a public_key column value.
Confirmed reachable: frontend CatalogBrowser/PluginManager components call this exact endpoint.
Git history confirms a solid, devmode-gated, fail-closed signature pipeline was built later (2026-04-13) for the CLI install path; this handler was never migrated onto it.
Zero test coverage for this handler at all.
findings.recommendation: Route handleCatalogInstall through the same pipeline the CLI already uses (internal/plugin/install.Installer + install.SignatureVerifier + catalog.SignedFetcher/KeyRing), which fail closed by default.

findings.summary: handleCatalogInstall also has an unconfined path-traversal write: target := filepath.Join(cs.pluginsDir, entry.Name) uses a plain filepath.Join (not pathsafe.ResolveUnder) where entry.Name comes from an untrusted catalog.yaml. Sibling handlers in the same file were already fixed for this exact bug class.
evidence: catalog.go:301: target := filepath.Join(cs.pluginsDir, entry.Name); :427: copyDir(pluginRoot, target).
handleInstall/handleInstallLocal (plugins.go) both already use pathsafe.ResolveUnder with inline comments citing 'audit finding: Critical -- path traversal'.
findings.recommendation: Apply pathsafe.ResolveUnder(cs.pluginsDir, entry.Name) at line 301, matching the pattern already used in the sibling handlers.
findings.false_positive_considerations: The archive-extraction step itself IS soundly defended -- the vulnerable point is specifically the final copyDir from the safely-extracted temp dir to the unguarded final target.

findings.summary: Two full parallel 'fetch catalog -> verify -> download -> extract -> install' implementations exist side by side -- the weaker one (feeding the vulnerable API handler) and the stronger, devmode-gated one (feeding only the CLI). Direct architectural cause of GO-PLUGIN-001/002.
findings.recommendation: Converge the API handler onto the stronger pipeline; retire the old CatalogFetcher/VerifyChecksum/VerifySignature once the caller is migrated (no other callers today).

findings.summary: UnloadPlugin (cyclomatic 63, 346 lines): essential complexity dominates (documented 18-category lock-disciplined teardown sweep), but ~10 categories are still hand-inlined map-iterate-delete logic that could be extracted like the other ~8 already are. Separately, a real narrow TOCTOU gap: a concurrent LoadPlugin(B) where B depends on the plugin being unloaded can pass its own dependency check in the window before the unload completes.
evidence: host.go:1240-1585; dependency check at 1249-1260 under lock, p.Unload() at 1264 runs lock-free by design (to avoid deadlock on re-entrant plugin calls).
findings.recommendation: Extract remaining inlined categories into small sweepXByPlugin helpers mirroring the established pattern; consider an unloading-in-progress guard to close the TOCTOU window if concurrent load/unload of interdependent plugins is a scenario worth defending.

findings.summary: validateCrossRefs (cyclomatic 35, 126 lines) is mechanically repetitive (9 near-identical per-section uniqueness checks) but not incorrect -- a guide §5 'may be clearer than fragmented helpers' case.
findings.recommendation: Optional: a generic checkUniqueKeys[T] helper could collapse ~80 lines with no behavior change; not urgent.

findings.summary: Host has 38 fields / 123 methods across 9 files, above both guide thresholds, but is a single coherent domain ('everything a plugin can register'). ~1/4 of registration categories are already extracted into dedicated sub-registry types with their own locks; the rest remain raw maps.
findings.recommendation: The established sub-registry pattern (cardRulesRegistry, panelRegistry, FilterRegistry, MutablePluginMux) is the natural extension path if the architect wants to reduce Host's footprint.

findings.summary: 4 CLI-ecosystem adapter plugins duplicate ~35-45 lines each of manifest-loading/registration/lifecycle boilerplate, byte-for-byte aside from names/strings.
findings.recommendation: A shared plugin.LoadEmbeddedManifest/plugin.BasePlugin helper could remove most of it without touching per-adapter logic.

findings.summary: user_settings.allow_unsigned_plugins is stored and API-exposed but never actually wired into the CLI signature verifier -- SignatureVerifier.AllowUnsigned is left at its zero-value false at the one production construction site, despite verify.go's doc comment describing the setting as the intended wiring.
evidence: grep confirms zero production `AllowUnsigned: true` assignments anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Wire user_settings.AllowUnsignedPlugins into buildInstaller's SignatureVerifier construction, or update the doc comments to stop claiming this wiring exists.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Opposite-direction of a security risk (stricter than documented, not weaker).

findings.summary: internal/tool's canonical Tool-interface/builder architecture is entirely dead (every exported symbol deadcode-flagged); only ResultCache is live. tool.go's package doc still actively claims this is 'the primary way to construct tools in Go code' -- false of the current runtime.
evidence: A prior task's own comment in internal/service/tool_concurrency_classification.go already reached this conclusion and left it in place.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the architect whether this represents an abandoned migration (delete) or a planned future direction (update the doc comment to say so explicitly).

findings.summary: Reasoning-augmented tool selection (RankTools/SelectWithSignals/SelectToolsAugmented) is dead in the production request path -- its former consumer (a debug SQL row) was removed by an earlier task. Explains 2 of the base report's previously-unjudged complexity outliers.
evidence: ranking.go:292-297's own comment documents the removal; the real production selection entry point (SelectToolsAsProvider) does not call this path.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether reasoning-augmented selection is a planned re-activation or an abandoned experiment; remove the dead code and its per-boot wiring cost (skills-dir load, memory-recaller construction) if abandoned.

findings.summary: tool_knowledge.go's entire curated-catalog intent-matching mechanism (405 lines) has zero callers -- a third parallel 'what tools match this intent' mechanism alongside the live intent.go keyword scorer and the dead RankTools.
findings.recommendation: Confirm dead, then remove.

findings.summary: elicitation.go's package doc describes a client-side direction (ClientElicitMiddleware) that does not exist anywhere in the codebase -- purely aspirational documentation. The functions implementing that direction are confirmed dead under both normal and -test reachability.
findings.recommendation: Either build the missing ClientElicitMiddleware or delete the client-side functions and correct the package doc.

findings.summary: Per-turn tool-name context is written every single tool dispatch (real production caller) but the reader has zero callers -- small but needless per-call cost; the write side's own comment frames this as deliberate scaffolding.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the write side or track it in a doc so it isn't rediscovered as dead code and cleaned up out of ignorance of the plan.

findings.summary: SelfToolsTransport is the strongest god-object candidate in this cluster: 31 fields, 81 methods, a single flat CallTool switch dispatching to ~62 tool names spanning ~15 largely-unrelated capability domains, implemented as real 2,431-line business logic, not thin adapters.
findings.recommendation: Assess whether tool-domain families (todo/plan, messaging, subagent-dispatch, workflow, panels, python, learning) could be split into per-domain handler sets composed into SelfToolsTransport.

findings.summary: ToolClient has 26 methods across 4 files backing 3 self-described responsibilities ('selection, permissions, and execution').
findings.recommendation: No action implied; record for the architect's holistic pass.

findings.summary: callGrep's gosec G122 hit is real: resolveAllowed correctly validates the top-level dir argument once (symlink-aware) before the walk begins, but the filepath.Walk callback then calls os.Open on every discovered file with no per-entry re-validation or symlink check -- a symlink inside an already-granted directory would leak file content outside the grant boundary.
evidence: dev_tools.go:690-871, os.Open at line 779 inside the walk callback.
findings.recommendation: Exclude symlinked entries in the walk, or re-run pathsafe.ResolveUnder per discovered file before os.Open.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Requires either write access to the granted directory or a pre-existing malicious symlink -- a local-filesystem TOCTOU class, not remotely triggerable via MCP input.

findings.summary: Manager.RemoveServer holds the registry-wide lock for the full duration of subprocess kill+reap (no timeout) -- every other Manager operation for unrelated MCP servers queues behind the same lock while one server tears down.
findings.recommendation: Consider releasing the manager lock before calling closer.Close().

findings.summary: Self-documented, deliberately independent second evaluation of the same dispatch_to_agent reflex rows -- the code's own comment argues this is intentional (two genuinely different decision points), though nothing tests that the two evaluators can never diverge.
findings.recommendation: Record for architect awareness; consider a test asserting the two evaluators stay in sync.

findings.summary: DevServerName = "dev" independently declared in both internal/mcp and internal/toolclient, despite the latter already importing the former.
findings.recommendation: Reference mcp.DevServerName directly.

findings.summary: Manager.ExecuteTool/ExecuteToolOnServer textually duplicate the entire post-CallTool result-processing pipeline (assemble, validate size, span attributes); both call sites are genuinely necessary, only the shared tail is duplicated.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared post-CallTool pipeline into a private helper both functions call.

findings.summary: mcpconfig.Export silently drops 2 json.Unmarshal errors on stored Args/Env -- part of the base report's already-tracked errcheck cluster, cited here with a precise location.
evidence: mcpconfig.go:145,150.
findings.recommendation: Log at slog.Warn on unmarshal failure.

findings.summary: Agent slug is never validated for path-safety before being joined into a managed-config file path, on both create and update. Full traced chain from POST /api/agents through ValidateAgentConfig (never references Slug) to ManagedAgentPath's plain filepath.Join to atomicWriteFile.
evidence: ManagedAgentPath (managed_files.go:87-95): filepath.Join(configRoot, 'agents', slug+'.md') with no character allow-list, no traversal rejection.
agentvalidation.ValidateAgentConfig never references Slug anywhere in its body.
handleUpdateAgent's rename path has no 'already exists' guard, so a crafted slug can OVERWRITE an existing arbitrary *.md file, not just create one.
A slug-format allow-list regex already exists elsewhere (internal/builders/agent_builder.go) gating a different endpoint -- never applied to the direct CRUD endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Validate Slug against a strict allow-list (mirroring the existing regex) inside ValidateAgentConfig or at the top of AgentConfigService.Create/Update, before ManagedAgentPath is ever called.
findings.false_positive_considerations: The final path component is always .md-suffixed, constraining (not eliminating) real-world impact. HTTP-layer auth boundary on POST/PUT /api/agents was not independently verified.

findings.summary: Every function in managed_files.go and source_class.go is at 0.0% test coverage, including Classification.IsWritablePath, the codebase's own trust-boundary gate for 'is this a writable managed path'. Directly tied to GO-AGENT-001 -- a fix currently has no safety net.
evidence: coverage-func.log confirms 0.0% for every function in both files; no test file exists for either.
findings.recommendation: Add direct unit tests for ManagedAgentPath/WriteManagedAgentProfile (including a traversal-rejection case once GO-AGENT-001 is fixed) and for Classification.Classify/IsWritablePath.

findings.summary: 3 exported symbols (EnsureManagedDirs, UserManagedAgentPath, ValidationResult.Error) confirmed unreachable under both normal and -test reachability.
findings.recommendation: Confirm not part of an external/plugin-consumed API surface, then remove or add the intended caller.

findings.summary: permissions_test.go's only remaining tests (after a prior removal task) test an unrelated concern (ParentDispatchAllowlist), not permissions -- stale filename.
findings.recommendation: Rename to parent_dispatch_allowlist_test.go or fold into convert_test.go.

findings.summary: A devmode-only builtin agent still stamps the legacy Source='builtin' value the sibling package's own doc says is retired -- traced the consequence: this profile falls through to ManageClassManaged (GUI/API-editable) instead of the hidden/read-only treatment every other embedded harness profile gets. Devmode-only blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Change embed_mux_devmode.go:21 to stamp SourceInternal to match the rest of the package's convention.

findings.summary: Three independent packages each hold their own separate copy of the shared *envelopes.Registry pointer, requiring main.go to remember 3 manual setter calls with nothing enforcing they stay in sync.
findings.recommendation: Consider a single shared registry holder rather than three independently-set copies, especially before any future hot-reload/test-isolation feature is added.

findings.summary: chat.replayContent and recovery/pack.MessagePlainText implement the identical StructuredMessage-JSON-unwrap algorithm -- one using the full shared type, the other a hand-rolled anonymous struct re-deriving the same two fields. Self-documented as intentional (avoiding a cross-package import) but the reviewer found no actual cycle risk in that direction.
findings.recommendation: Consider exporting a minimal shared unwrap helper both packages call, after confirming the import-cycle constraint is real.

findings.summary: service_test_helpers.go has no _test.go suffix, so it compiles into the production binary -- including elicitWithDuration, a near line-for-line reimplementation of Elicit's body that could silently diverge from real Elicit behavior.
findings.recommendation: Rename to export_test.go pattern so it's excluded from production builds.

findings.summary: ElicitUserInput/routeClientElicitation are near-duplicate ~25-line bodies with inconsistent context.Canceled handling -- one swallows it into a graceful cancel result, the other surfaces it as both a cancel payload and a non-nil error.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared 'call Elicit, translate to response' logic into one helper both call, or document why the two paths need different error contracts.

findings.summary: PrefixLock/PrefixState/LockTTL declared with zero consumers anywhere -- a planned-but-never-built 'resource lock' feature layered on CoordStore.
findings.recommendation: Either wire an actual lock-acquire/release helper, or remove until the feature is built.

findings.summary: hint_catalog.go's package doc claims the loader reads config/think-hints/hints.yaml; the actual go:embed directive embeds a different file. The two are currently byte-identical but no build step copies one into the other.
findings.recommendation: Fix the doc comment to point at the real embedded path, or add a generate/build step if the config/ file is meant to be an editable source of truth.

findings.summary: 12 files in this cluster fail gofmt -l (part of the pre-existing repo-wide 122-file gap already covered by GO-HYG-001).
findings.recommendation: gofmt -w is safe and mechanical; batchable with the repo-wide cleanup.

findings.summary: internal/chat's wide fan-out (11 internal packages) mixes broadly-consumed wire-vocabulary types with subsystem-specific response-handler wiring in the same package -- not a cycle, but means a caller wanting only Envelope/ResponseV1 transitively depends on the entire subagent+elicitation+mcp+plugin graph anyway.
findings.recommendation: Consider whether subsystem-specific response handlers belong in their own thin wiring files/subpackage separate from the pure-vocabulary core.

findings.summary: Elicit's three-way select has a theoretical response/timeout race inherent to any select-based timeout; negligible at production's 5-minute default, proportionally larger (still very unlikely) at the sub-second timeouts the GO-CHAT-003 test helper uses.
findings.recommendation: None recommended; recorded for completeness.

findings.summary: Approve() bypasses the fan-out concurrency semaphore entirely -- Spawn's ungated paths correctly acquire a slot from the documented cap-of-3 semaphore before dispatching, but Approve launches its dispatch goroutine directly with no slot acquisition. Multiple approvals in quick succession can drive concurrently-executing runners past the stated cap.
evidence: service.go: Spawn's acquireSpawnSlot calls vs. Approve's direct goroutine launch with no acquisition.
findings.recommendation: Route Approve's dispatch through executeWithSlot (acquiring the slot before or as part of approval), or explicitly document the exemption.

findings.summary: A run cancelled while still queued for a spawn slot is not actually stopped -- only relabeled after it finishes running anyway. The cancellation hook is only registered after the slot is acquired, but the run is broadcast as 'running' before that.
evidence: Traced: emitStatus broadcasts 'running' before acquireSpawnSlot; cancelers[run.ID] only registered after slot acquisition; finalizeRun's re-read reconciliation eventually corrects the terminal status but the run itself was not interrupted.
findings.recommendation: Register a lightweight 'queued' cancellation hook before acquireSpawnSlot is attempted, or re-check the row's current status immediately after acquiring a slot before invoking the runner.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Data integrity is not at risk -- finalizeRun's reconciliation correctly prevents a stale/wrong terminal status; only the run itself proceeds when it shouldn't.

findings.summary: Three 'workflow'-branded packages implement three different execution models. The maintainers were already aware (agentworkflow/doc.go explicitly documents why it wasn't nested as a workflow subpackage) -- deliberate, not an oversight, but still a real grep/mental-model cost.
findings.recommendation: No action required beyond continued awareness.

findings.summary: internal/dispatch vs internal/dispatcher -- similar names, genuinely different well-documented concepts.
findings.recommendation: No rename recommended without architect review; flagged for awareness only.

findings.summary: internal/grounding's entire pre-strategy memory-recall subsystem is fully built and tested but never wired in production -- GroundingRecaller/GroundingLogger fields exist on the self-tools transport, but zero production code anywhere constructs and assigns a *grounding.Recaller to them.
evidence: deadcode + exhaustive grep confirm zero production assignment; also gated behind an env var defaulting off.
findings.recommendation: Either wire GroundingRecaller/GroundingLogger into the composition root, or treat as an abandoned Phase-5 feature and schedule removal.

findings.summary: contextbroker/gate_hadron_blueprints.go's entire ContextGate/HadronBlueprintGate is confirmed entirely dead, and contains a latent unbounded-relevance-score bug (additive scoring with no clamp against a documented 0.0-1.0 contract) that would corrupt cross-source ranking if ever revived unfixed.
evidence: Never registered as a ContextSource in the composition root, unlike its 4 live siblings; calculateRelevance sums up to 6 bonuses with no clamp.
findings.recommendation: Remove if genuinely abandoned, or fix the unbounded scoring before wiring in if reviving.

findings.summary: BudgetForIntent/IntentSourcePriority unused (a second, dead budget-allocation strategy); DefaultBudget()'s SourceWeights includes an 'engine': 0.15 entry with no backing ContextSource implementation anywhere in the repo -- inert, misleading configuration.
findings.recommendation: Remove BudgetForIntent/IntentSourcePriority if superseded; drop the 'engine' weight entry or implement the promised EngineSource.

findings.summary: Each contextbroker source computes ContextItem.Relevance via an unrelated method yet all are merged and cross-compared on one global scale with no shared contract beyond 'roughly 0-1'.
findings.recommendation: Document/enforce a shared relevance-normalization contract before merging cross-source lists.

findings.summary: Two independent 'chars/4' token-estimation formulas (one floors, one always rounds up) measure the same content at two different stages of the same budget pipeline, diverging by a few tokens for any length not a multiple of 4.
findings.recommendation: Converge on one estimator; contextbroker's deliberate one-way dependency away from internal/context means this would need a shared lower-level package.

findings.summary: Detector.windows map has no production eviction path -- Reset(sessionID) exists specifically for this but has zero production callers; for a long-running daemon, every distinct session that ever calls a tool adds a permanent entry.
findings.recommendation: Call Detector.Reset(sessionID) on session end, or add a bounded LRU/TTL eviction inside Detector itself.

findings.summary: orphansweep.SweepOrphans is dead in production (bypassed by RuntimeReaper.SweepOnce calling the inner function directly), but multiple other files' doc comments still describe it as the live entry point.
findings.recommendation: Delete the now-redundant SweepOrphans wrapper, or update the stale cross-file doc comments.

findings.summary: recovery/broker's With* constructor options are deadcode-flagged but the equivalent Set* post-construction setters exist for a documented, legitimate late-binding reason -- recorded specifically so a future reviewer doesn't re-flag this as real dead code.
findings.recommendation: No action needed; example of the guide's own 'reported dead != remove' guardrail working correctly.

findings.summary: RuntimeReaper's sweep function explicitly discards its own ctx parameter (_ = ctx), so an in-flight DB call cannot be cancelled mid-flight by the shutdown signal -- Stop() simply blocks until that call returns on its own.
findings.recommendation: Propagate ctx into the underlying DB calls so shutdown can cancel an in-flight sweep.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Low risk in practice -- local SQLite call, bounded.

findings.summary: On Linux, if bwrap (bubblewrap) isn't installed, applyOSSandbox silently falls back to no OS-level isolation and returns success -- AgentExec treats this identically to a real sandbox being applied. Re-confirmed still-open from the 2026-04-10 dedicated sandbox-hardening audit.
evidence: os_linux.go:64-71: LookPath failure logs a warn once and returns func(){}, nil (success shape) rather than an error; AgentExec proceeds unsandboxed.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed by default on Linux (return an error rather than a warning) with an explicit opt-out env var for CI/dev.
findings.false_positive_considerations: None -- direct re-confirmation against current source.

findings.summary: Linux network allowlist is not enforced at the OS/namespace level in proxy mode -- when NetworkAllow is non-empty, the sandboxed process keeps the host's network namespace; confinement relies entirely on HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env-var convention, which any tool can ignore.
evidence: os_linux.go:132-148: --unshare-net only applied when networkAllow is empty.
findings.recommendation: Enforce egress at the namespace level (co-locate the proxy inside the sandbox netns, or a veth/socket-passing approach), or explicitly document/gate proxy-mode network access as reduced-guarantee.
findings.false_positive_considerations: macOS is unaffected -- seatbelt's network-outbound deny is real and kernel-enforced.

findings.summary: permission.Engine's ModeDefault doesn't actually ask before non-destructive writes, contradicting its own doc comment ('prompt for destructive/write operations') -- dev_write/dev_edit match neither the read-only nor destructive name-heuristic pattern, so both flags resolve false, and ModeDefault's switch has no {false,false} branch (falls through to Allow). ModeAcceptEdits has the missing branch right next to it.
evidence: engine.go:156-180; untested exact case: the existing test table doesn't cover ToolMeta{} under ModeDefault.
findings.recommendation: Confirm intended architecture (PathGrants-governs-writability vs. per-call-prompt) with the architect before changing; if a real gap, classify dev_write/dev_edit as destructive or add the missing branch to ModeDefault.
findings.false_positive_considerations: PathGrants' own documented design philosophy ('explicit-mention auto-grant, no nag-again') may mean this is a stale-comment issue, not a live regression.

findings.summary: Secret-key-name substring heuristic still misses DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, GH_PAT, and other credential-bearing names that don't contain the tracked substrings. Unchanged from the 2026-04-10 audit finding.
findings.recommendation: Combine the substring heuristic with an exact-match hard-deny list for known credential-bearing *_URL/*_TOKEN-adjacent names, or switch AgentExec's overlay to an explicit allowlist model.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Highest-risk surface is AgentExec (agent/LLM-influenced code), not UserExec (user's own shell).

findings.summary: macOS seatbelt profile stays (allow default) for file reads/mach-IPC/process-inspection by design -- tracked, deliberate beta-stage tradeoff from the 2026-04-10 audit, not new. Restated for visibility alongside GO-SEC4-002 (both platforms leave the read boundary unenforced by design).
findings.recommendation: Confirm this tradeoff is disclosed to end users; not re-litigated in full here.

findings.summary: Command denylist remains a bypassable literal-substring blocklist (whitespace variation, flag reordering, or interpreter wrapping all defeat it). Low severity in isolation but becomes the ONLY remaining control on Linux without bwrap (GO-SEC4-001).
findings.recommendation: Reframe in comments as advisory/defense-in-depth rather than a hard block, or replace with real shell-tokenization.

findings.summary: SSRF-defense CIDR denylist is independently duplicated between internal/sandbox/proxy.go and internal/mcp/general_tools.go, with the sandbox copy's own comment stating the intent is parity -- but nothing enforces that parity mechanically. If one is updated and the other isn't, the two egress paths silently drift apart.
findings.recommendation: Extract the shared CIDR set into one place both packages import, or add a test that asserts the two lists are identical.

findings.summary: Sandbox proxy's http.Server has no ReadHeaderTimeout (gosec G112, Slowloris). Real exposure is narrow (loopback-only bind, reachable only by the sandboxed subprocess itself) but it's a zero-risk one-line fix.
findings.recommendation: Set ReadHeaderTimeout (e.g. 10s) on the http.Server.

findings.summary: make lint-goroutines's scanned-package list omits every package in this trust-boundary cluster; manually confirmed the one bare go func() found in scope is benign, but the guardrail tooling itself doesn't cover this cluster.
findings.recommendation: Add these five packages to lint-goroutines's scanned path list.

findings.summary: secrets.Get collapses key-not-found and keychain-access-error into the identical silent empty-string return with no logging, unlike its sibling Delete which does log on failure.
findings.recommendation: Log at debug/warn on the error path, or return (string, error) for callers that need to distinguish.

findings.summary: cmdServe's slogx.Fatal exit paths (os.Exit(1), doesn't run deferred functions) bypass every deferred cleanup registered earlier in the function -- log-handler close, OTel flush, SQLite store close, Badger coordination-store close -- on 5 real startup-failure call sites.
findings.recommendation: Replace slogx.Fatal on these 5 call sites with return/structured propagation so the existing defers execute, or make slogx.Fatal accept a cleanup-hook slice.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Bounded blast radius -- process always terminates immediately after, no accumulating leak.

findings.summary: Auth is entirely opt-in via env vars (no-op middleware if unset), the listener binds all interfaces by default (no loopback-only option exists), no TLS anywhere, and no startup-time log line announces whether auth is enabled or disabled.
evidence: caller_identity.go explicitly documents this as an intentional design decision for a single-user local app.
findings.recommendation: Consider defaulting the listener to 127.0.0.1 unless an explicit bind-all opt-in is set, and/or log a clear startup warning when auth is unconfigured.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Substantial documented-intent caveat: an architect may reasonably judge the current tradeoff acceptable for this product's deployment model.

findings.summary: worktree.gitManager.CleanupOrphaned computes the wrong (8-char-truncated) branch name and therefore never deletes the actual orphaned git branch Create made with the full ULID session ID -- runs on every daemon boot, so every cleanup leaves a permanent stray branch, accumulating unboundedly across restarts/crashes.
evidence: manager.go:86 (Create, full sessionID) vs :166-170 (CleanupOrphaned, truncated to 8 chars); existing regression test only asserts directory removal, never that the branch is gone.
findings.recommendation: CleanupOrphaned should reconstruct the branch name identically to Create (full sessionID, no truncation).

findings.summary: background.Service/PTYBackend job registries grow unboundedly for the process's entire lifetime -- every job that starts stays in the map forever except one narrow immediate-failure path; jobRecord retains up to 1 MiB of captured output per job indefinitely. PTYBackend.Status's own doc comment falsely claims completed jobs are 'reaped'.
findings.recommendation: Add a TTL/LRU eviction policy for terminal jobs, or explicitly acknowledge unbounded retention is intentional for this MVP scope and fix the inaccurate comment either way.
findings.false_positive_considerations: Real-world impact scales with background_job submission volume, which was not measured.

findings.summary: service.Container.Shutdown has no idempotency guard at all, unlike its sibling lifecycle.Manager.Shutdown which is correctly idempotent. Currently dormant (exactly one production call site).
findings.recommendation: Add the same sync.Once/atomic-bool guard lifecycle.Manager.Shutdown already uses, for consistency and defense-in-depth.

findings.summary: Systemic ticket-archaeology comment density across this cluster -- cmdServe is roughly half comment-lines to code-lines. Not a functional defect; some content is genuinely load-bearing invariant documentation.
findings.recommendation: An architect-level pass (not mechanical stripping) could migrate pure-history portions to docs/decisions/.

findings.summary: loadPersistedMCPServers silently discards 2 of 3 JSON decode errors on persisted MCP server config (Args, Env) while correctly warn-logging the third (EnvAllowlist) right next to them in the same function -- a malformed persisted row silently launches with empty args/env.
evidence: main.go:1233-1277: Args/Env unmarshal errors discarded, EnvAllowlist's is correctly warn-logged.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same check-and-warn pattern used for EnvAllowlist to Args/EnvVars.

findings.summary: agent.Boot is the second-highest cyclomatic complexity function in the entire codebase (50/cognitive 59, maintainability index 10, 234 lines) -- missed by the mechanical triage table and this cluster's pre-flagged list; judged essential, same shape as cmdServe, with a correctly-applied cleanup closure at every early-return point.
evidence: Should be added to the master complexity/Top-10 tracking alongside cmdServe/UnloadPlugin/Executor.Run/Service.Spawn.
findings.recommendation: No fix required -- essential complexity, correctly handled. Optional readability extraction of 2 cohesive sub-blocks noted, not required.
